Worker follow-ups: memory cap on Linux, DELETE /jobs/<id> with a retention note, cancel endpoint and per-episode progress
items.note: DELETE /jobs/<id>, cancel and delete buttons, episode progress and an optional memory cap. The memory cap counts resident memory: the worker reads the job's process tree every 0.5 s and kills it past ARRIVAL_MAX_JOB_MB with a MemoryLimitError naming the stage (#192). The old RLIMIT_AS cap followed the core count and crashed jobs (docs/ref/MEMCAP.md).

items.title: Real GR00T loader check and fine-tune on hero_kitchen_sim
items.note: GR00T N1.7-3B fine-tuned on one 96 GB GPU and scored in the sim on identical trials. Best 39 of 48 (81%) against 26 of 48 for the clean-data baseline (paired sign test p = 0.007): clean data plus DART demos with the marginal drawer pulls removed. Self-reported in #165 and #63; small samples, and the base-GR00T and generic-RoboCasa cells (G3, G4) are not run, so `usefulness` stays null. Weights: https://huggingface.co/Ish1105/arrival-gr00t-n17-run4 (NVIDIA Open Model License, not the repo's Apache 2.0). The same card reports clean plus unfiltered DART at 22 of 48. The fine-tunes ran on one 96 GB GPU on Cosmos, not on Nebius.

items.title: Nebius Serverless Jobs fan-out with resume, then one real small run
items.note: Fan-out with done-markers, retry and resume is built. arrival fanout --backend nebius runs shards as Serverless AI Jobs with an Object Storage bucket, tested only against in-process fakes of both APIs. It has never run against Nebius. The hackathon rules count a project as running on Nebius only if it calls the Token Factory inference API or runs on Nebius AI Cloud (Serverless Jobs, Serverless Endpoints, or DevPods). Neither has been done.

The static site is still undeployed: cd site && vercel --prod, then put the live URL in the README and on the form if you submit one. #195 checked http://localhost:8765 at 1024 px and 375 px in both themes.

groups.title: Devpost form
groups.blurb: Nebius x NVIDIA Global AI Hackathon, https://nebiusglobalaihackathon.devpost.com/. Deadline Friday, October 30, 2026, 10:00am Pacific. Physical AI is the track: a demo URL is not required, and with no robot the video needs at least one minute of the key modules (P4).

items.title: Fill the Devpost form: Physical AI, description, public repo, and feedback
items.note: Required on the form: the track, a text description of what it is, why, and how it works, a public GitHub URL whose About section shows the Apache 2.0 license, a README with setup instructions, the YouTube link (P4), and written feedback on Token Factory, AI Cloud, and the NVIDIA models used. Highlight GR00T and any Nemotron or Token Factory use. English. A demo URL is optional on this track (C2). If the project existed before August 26, 2026, say what changed during the submission period. The project has to run as the video and the text describe, and the rules require a real Token Factory call or a Nebius AI Cloud run (C1).
